page: Google Cloud Platform x4-960-16t-metal is a high-capacity bare-metal server belonging to the memory-optimized family. It provides 960 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture, coupled with 16,384 GB of total system RAM. This configuration establishes an allocation of approximately 17.07 GB of memory per processing core. The platform operates without integrated graphics accelerators or GPUs, focusing physical resources entirely on central processing and system memory capacity.

The server includes no bundled local storage, requiring external networked block storage solutions to support system volumes and persistent data operations. Network provisioning includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because the instance is provisioned as bare metal, workloads execute directly on the physical host without hypervisor virtualization layers, eliminating hypervisor overhead and resource contention.

In qualitative terms, the resource density of x4-960-16t-metal reflects an extreme single-node scale-up profile. Cost efficiency requires maximizing utilization of the vast 16 TB memory pool, as underutilization of either the 960 physical cores or the RAM footprint introduces substantial operational waste. Primary workload fits include very large enterprise in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, large-scale transaction processing systems, and complex memory-resident data analytics.
description: Google Cloud Platform x4-960-16t-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server configured with 960 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 16,384 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 17.07 GB of memory per core. The platform features no integrated GPUs and includes no bundled local storage, necessitating external storage volumes for persistent data operations. Networking configurations allocate zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Engineered for maximum physical density and extensive capacity requirements, x4-960-16t-metal eliminates virtualization overhead via dedicated bare-metal access. The massive memory footprint makes it an infrastructure choice tailored for scale-up architectures rather than distributed scale-out nodes. Due to its extensive resource allocation, it represents a capital-heavy profile suited strictly for mission-critical enterprise deployments where data must reside continuously in RAM. The instance fits ultra-large in-memory database engines, massive SAP HANA instances, and vast real-time analytics platforms.
